newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies open mixed as mark, yen diverge.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies open mixed as mark, yen diverge.

text.p: IMM currency futures opened mixed, with yen firm on expectations for strong Japanese current account surplus data tonight but European currencies weakening amid ongoing dollar buying, traders said.
The divergent price trends were causing nervousness in currencies across the board, said an IMM floor analyst.

Market participants are valuing the dollar higher versus the mark and Swiss franc as the robust U.S. economy continues to draw overseas investors to U.S. assets, keeping dollars in high demand, the analyst said.

Concern the German and Swiss central banks could follow Australia's lead and sell gold reserves to take advantage of the low-inflation environment was also weighing on the European currencies, the analyst said.
Australia's central bank last week said it had sold 167 metric tonnes of gold this year.
Mark futures made a new contract low of $0.5718 in overnight trading and was hovering near that level early in the pit session.
The IMM analyst predicted mark futures could decline to $0.5703, equivalent to about 1.7618 in spot dollar/mark, but cautioned that yen strength could counteract dollar bullishness.
"I'm afraid dollar/yen weakness is going to pull this market the other way," he said.
Yen futures push higher early amid expectations for a strong May Japan current account surplus figure to be released tonight, on the heels of a sharp rise in the 20-day June trade surplus data.

Market participants interpreted overnight comments from Eisuke Sakakibara, Japan's director general of the International Finance Bureau of the Ministry of Finance, as an attempt to talk up the dollar to mitigate the potential impact of the current account report. The dollar rose after Sakakibara said Japan's policy against using foreign exchange rates as as a trade tool had not changed.

British pounds opened firm after stronger than expected June UK retail price data bolstered the case for higher interest rates, but pressure from local traders who sold the futures in thin volume brought prices back down, traders said.

The UK data showed underlying inflation minus mortgage payments running at a 2.7 percent annualized rate, up from May's 2.5 percent, which is the government's target. The headline retail price index rose 2.9 percent year over year, also exceeding expectations. The Bank of England's policy committee is meeting Wednesday and Thursday.

September yen was up $0.000019 at $0.008975, marks were down $0.0022 at $0.5718, Swiss francs fell $0.0027 at $0.6880, sterling was down $0.0014 at $1.6860, Canadian dollars were up $0.0012 at $0.7306, Australian dollars were up $0.0029 at $0.7475 and Mexican pesos rose $0.000050 at $0.122950. ((Chicago Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
